note.explanation: Alkanes can be prepared by cracking larger hydrocarbons, adding hydrogen to alkenes or alkynes, or reducing alkyl halides.
examples: Ethene + hydrogen → ethane, using nickel at 200°C.
note.checkAnswer: Add hydrogen to the alkene or alkyne in the presence of nickel at 200°C.
note.simple: There are three methods in this section: break large hydrocarbons into smaller ones, add hydrogen to an unsaturated hydrocarbon, or replace the halogen in an alkyl halide with hydrogen.
note.checkQuestion: How can an alkene be changed into an alkane?
note.title: Preparation of Alkanes
steps: For cracking, heat naphtha to around 500°C with zeolite.
For hydrogenation, add hydrogen to an alkene or alkyne with nickel as catalyst at 200°C.
For reduction of an alkyl halide, use hydrogen produced by zinc reacting with hydrochloric acid.
note.answer: Alkanes are prepared by cracking higher hydrocarbons, reducing alkenes or alkynes with hydrogen, or reducing alkyl halides with hydrogen generated using Zn/HCl.

mcqs.stem: Which conditions are used to crack naphtha into smaller hydrocarbons?
rationales: This is correct: naphtha is heated at around 500°C in the presence of zeolite.
Cooling without a catalyst is not the cracking method described.
Adding water is not the method described for cracking naphtha.
Burning naphtha is combustion, not cracking.

mcqs.stem: Which catalyst is used when hydrogen is added to an alkene to prepare an alkane?
rationales: Copper is not the catalyst specified for this hydrogenation method.
This is correct: nickel is used as the catalyst in the hydrogenation of alkenes and alkynes.
Sodium chloride is not the catalyst specified for this reaction.
Zeolite is used in cracking, not in the hydrogenation method described.

mcqs.stem: Which alkane cannot be prepared by reducing an alkene or alkyne with hydrogen?
rationales: This is correct: the textbook states that methane cannot be prepared by this method.
Ethane can be prepared by hydrogenating ethene or ethyne.
Propane can be prepared by hydrogenating an appropriate unsaturated hydrocarbon.
Butane can be prepared by hydrogenating an appropriate unsaturated hydrocarbon.

mcqs.stem: How many hydrogen molecules are shown reacting with ethyne to form ethane?
rationales: One H₂ molecule is not enough for the reaction shown.
This is correct: the reaction shown is CH≡CH + 2H₂ → CH₃—CH₃.
Three H₂ molecules are more than the equation requires.
Four H₂ molecules are more than the equation requires.

options: Hydrogen from zinc and hydrochloric acid
Oxygen from zinc and hydrochloric acid
Chlorine from zinc and hydrochloric acid
Water from zinc and hydrochloric acid
mcqs.stem: What is used to reduce an alkyl halide to an alkane in the method described?
rationales: This is correct: hydrogen generated by the reaction of zinc with hydrochloric acid reduces the alkyl halide.
Oxygen is not the reducing agent in this method.
Chlorine is not used to reduce the alkyl halide.
Water is not the reducing agent specified in the method.

mcqs.stem: What change occurs when an alkyl halide is reduced to an alkane?
rationales: This would form an alcohol, not the alkane shown in the section.
This is correct: the halogen-containing group R—X is reduced to R—H.
This would join two R groups and is not the reaction given.
This would form an ether and is not the reaction given.

mcqs.stem: What type of reaction occurs when hydrogen is added to an unsaturated compound?
rationales: This is correct: an addition reaction occurs when hydrogen is added to an unsaturated compound.
Substitution is not the reaction type defined for adding hydrogen to an unsaturated compound.
Hydrogenation is the name of the process of adding hydrogen to alkenes or alkynes, but the reaction type asked for is addition.
Cracking breaks larger hydrocarbons into smaller hydrocarbons; it is not addition of hydrogen.

options: Smaller hydrocarbons that are more in demand
A single alkane with the same molecular mass
mcqs.stem: What is the purpose of cracking higher hydrocarbons?
rationales: This is correct: cracking breaks higher-molecular-mass hydrocarbons into smaller hydrocarbons that are more in demand.
Carbon dioxide and water are products of complete combustion, not cracking.
Cracking does not produce only hydrogen gas.
Cracking breaks the larger hydrocarbons into smaller hydrocarbons rather than making one alkane of the same molecular mass.

explain.title: Cracking higher hydrocarbons
explain.body: Cracking is the name of a process in which hydrocarbons with higher molecular masses (which are lesser in demand) are broken up into smaller hydrocarbons which are more in demand. This is done by heating the hydrocarbons at high temperature in the presence of a catalyst. Naphtha is heated at around 500°C with zeolite to give hydrocarbons with five to ten carbon atoms.

explain.title: Reducing alkenes and alkynes
explain.body: Alkanes can be prepared by reducing alkenes and alkynes with hydrogen gas in the presence of nickel metal as a catalyst. Methane cannot be prepared by this method. The reaction is also called hydrogenation of alkenes and alkynes and is an example of addition reaction. An addition reaction occurs when hydrogen (H₂) is added to an unsaturated compound.

explain.title: Reducing alkyl halides
explain.body: Alkyl halides (R-X) can be reduced to alkanes with hydrogen generated by reaction of zinc metal with hydrochloric acid. The textbook represents this hydrogen as [2H]: R—X + [2H] → R—H + H—X.

explain.title: Remember the reaction conditions
explain.body: For the displayed alkene and alkyne hydrogenation reactions, write Ni above the arrow and 200°C below it. For the alkyl-halide method, use Zn/HCl to generate [2H].

mistakes: Do not confuse cracking with combustion: cracking makes smaller hydrocarbons; combustion burns a hydrocarbon.
Do not leave out zeolite or the approximate 500°C condition when describing the cracking of naphtha.
Do not say methane can be prepared by hydrogenating an alkene or alkyne; the textbook states that it cannot be prepared by this method.
Do not forget that ethyne requires 2H₂ in the displayed reaction to form ethane.
In alkyl-halide reduction, do not omit H—X from the products or confuse [2H] with the catalyst.
